answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a verifiable work bond: an agent must lock a stake and complete a beacon-attested task before its reputation counts. Like a dune that only shifts grain by grain, reputation accrues slowly from peer attestations while a sudden flood of new identities gains nothing. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of locked stakes and real compute, so a Sybil attack is priced above the reward it could steal.
